title: Provider, payer and settlement reconciliation controls
summary: Selected controls prevent duplicated capitation revenue, unsupported patient billing and mixed claim/PLB or charity populations.
jurisdiction: United States; selected provider, payer and entity roles

provenance.reviewer: Codex AI-assisted bounded source and editorial review
provenance.scope: Selected primary-source passages and original synthetic provider worksheets; not professional verification.
provenance.note: Source-only proposal pending independent acceptance and current integration.

rights.external_content: External publisher text is not stored; publisher terms and source rights remain separate and unresolved.

controls: Stable encounter/claim/remittance/bank identifiers and duplicate detection
No patient balance transfer from a provider-responsibility code alone
Separate price concession, contractual adjustment, charity policy and credit-loss classification
EFT equals claim payment total plus or minus separately reconciled provider-level items
Provider/year-specific cost-report form and book-to-report mapping; no cost-equals-payment assumption
Member roster, service period, resident deposit and donor barrier checks; restricted data access
failure_conditions: Missing provider/payer identity, contract or role
Unmatched claim, EFT or provider-level adjustment
Unsupported estimate, denominator or source period
evidence: Provider identity, entity form, payer contract, patient policy and service dates
Encounter and claim identifiers, charges, allowed amounts, concession estimates and responsibility assignment
ERA line/claim adjustments, PLB details, claim references and EFT trace tied to bank
Member roster and covered period for capitation; resident contract and refundable deposit register
GL cost centers, cost-report form and fiscal year, MAC settlement and prior estimate
Award conditions, eligible units, return rights and donor restrictions; charity cost method and separate funding
limitations: Current consolidated ASC, later amendments, actual payer contracts, patient financial-assistance policy and provider-specific reporting obligations remain unverified.
Synthetic cases contain no patient data, live claims or actual cost reports; professional review and empirical performance are not established.
Publisher rights remain unknown and full text is not stored; selected roles do not establish whole-sector sufficiency or state-law coverage.
